newsitem.title: INDIA: Yield at India 91-day t-bill may dip, dealers say.
newsitem.headline: Yield at India 91-day t-bill may dip, dealers say.

text.p: The yield at the weekly auction of 91-day treasury bill on Friday evening may slip to 6.75-6.80 percent from last week's 7.02 percent, dealers said.
"We are expecting a yield of 6.7-6.8 percent because of good liquidity," said one money dealer at a leading foreign bank.
"I would say between 6.9 to 7.0 percent," said the head of money markets at a European bank in Bombay.
Dealers at two state-run banks said they saw a distinct possibility of yields easing as liquidity was comfortable.
The yield was steady at 6.77 percent at the four weekly auctions until June 6, but rose to 7.02 percent on June 13.
But a few bankers said they expected the yield to hold steady at seven percent level.
"The repo auction (on Thursday) has taken away 45 billion rupees," said R. Narayan, assistant treasury manager at Bank of Nova Scotia. "There is little enthusiasm to bid today."
He said Friday's 91-day treasury bill issue could devolve unless non-competitive bidders came to the rescue.
Narayan said three month commercial papers of blue-chip companies were quoted at 9.75 percent to 10.0 percent.
"These are very liquid assets," he said.
The manager (money markets) at another bank said the market appetite for three month money was above 7.0 percent.
"The RBI (Reserve Bank of India) has set the cut-off at an unrealistically low rate of less than 7.0 percent to fund the government's ways and means advances," he said.
A poll of company treasurers by Standard Chartered Bank showed the yield at the 91-day treasury bill at a mean of 6.76 percent in three months and 6.86 percent in six months.
"Treasurers see yields in the 91-day treasury bill moving up marginally, which is in divergence to what they expect with the bank's prime lending rates," it said in a commentary.
"This can be possibly be explained by the fact that they expect the surplus liquidity of the short-term to dry up a bit."
"That is already in tune with reality as the last cut-off for the 91-day treasury bill was at 7.02 percent."
Dealers said they expect a steady yield at 4.96 percent at Friday's 14-day treasury bills auction.
